card.title: Spread it out or cram it in?

body.question: In a 2006 review of memory studies, spaced practice was compared with massed practice (cramming) in 271 cases. How often did spaced practice come out ahead?
options: About two thirds of the time
body.reveal: Spaced practice beat massed practice in 259 of 271 cases. The gains are especially large when the gaps between sessions are days or weeks.

probes.question: Which study plan favours long-term memory?
options: One long session the night before
Several sessions spread over days or weeks

probes.question: Learning more by spreading study out in time is called the ____ effect.

image_brief.show: A planner or calendar page, e.g. File:Personal organizer with metallic ring binder.jpg, or students at a library table

claims.claim: 2006 study: spaced beat massed in 259 of 271 cases (question, reveal)
claims.quote: participants who used spaced practice on memory tasks outperformed those using massed practice in 259 out of 271 cases
claims.note: Page says Cepeda et al. (2006) 'study'; its reference title calls it a review and quantitative synthesis.

claims.claim: Gains are especially large when gaps are days or weeks (reveal)
claims.quote: long-term spacing effects are prevalent in learning and produce significant learning gains, particularly when the spacing gaps are on the order of days or weeks

claims.claim: Spreading study out in time is the spacing effect; favours long-term memory (probes)
claims.quote: Psychological effect that people learn more by spreading studying out in time
